content_of_post_to_comment: Everyone jokes about quitting corporate to open a bakery, work in a bookstore, or become a barista. I don’t think most people actually want easier work. They want work they can see. Something they can start. Something they can finish. Someone they can help. A point where they can say: I did that. The “little bakery” fantasy isn’t really about escaping responsibility, it’s about actually having a workday with a tangible end.
comment: Maybe the deeper divide isn't easy work vs hard work, but visible work vs abstract work. Modern jobs often hide completion, which can quietly erode the satisfaction of making something real.
